- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day moving avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 10-day moving avg as ceiling.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price at 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply a 1–2% upward bias for mixed sentiment periods.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33), model lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently misses true price by +2% or more, apply a downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per 10-day sentiment dip.
